headline:
An occasion
to come together.
intro: Seasonal food, generous tables, and the kind of hospitality that lets you be part of your own gathering.
serviceTitle: Made for the way you gather.
serviceIntro: Choose a style of hospitality before choosing individual dishes. These sample menus begin the conversation.

offers.title: The shared table
offers.text: A generous family-style spread that brings a room together.

offers.title: The easy gathering
offers.text: Beautifully arranged food for the occasions that want room to move.

offers.title: The working lunch
offers.text: A thoughtful midday menu for teams with a full agenda.

story.eyebrow: HOST WITH A LITTLE MORE EASE
story.title: The best seat should still be yours.
story.text: A gathering has a rhythm: arrival, conversation, food, and the moments between. A considered menu and service plan give you room to enjoy all of it.
points: A menu shaped around the occasion
Service, rentals, and cleanup made clear

guide.title: Every table has a different story.
guide.intro: Begin with the feeling of the gathering, the guest count, and the space. The menu comes into focus from there.

notes.title: At home
notes.text: An intimate dinner needs a plan for kitchen access, serving space, timing, and cleanup. Decide how much hosting support you want.

notes.title: A celebration
notes.text: Weddings, milestones, and welcome parties need a shared timeline with the venue. Confirm rentals, staffing, and access before finalizing service.

notes.title: At work
notes.text: Meeting schedules, delivery access, dietary labels, and serving windows shape a successful workplace meal. Decide whether the food is delivered, set up, or staffed.

notes.title: At the planning table
notes.text: Allergies, ingredient requirements, and shared preparation surfaces need a direct discussion with the caterer. Sample menu labels are not a safety guarantee.

faq.q: Can the menu adapt to dietary needs?
faq.a: A real caterer should review each requirement and explain what can be accommodated. The event brief collects topics for that discussion.
Not automatically. Service, tableware, rentals, setup, and cleanup should be itemized in a real proposal.

faq.q: Can I confirm an event here?
faq.a: No. This is a fictional example with illustrative menus and prices. The planner produces a sample brief only.

flow.title: Let’s set your table.
flow.intro: Shape a sample event brief around your people and your occasion.

steps.title: At the table
steps.intro: Choose a menu style and dietary discussion points.
